source: Media Report
acc_desc: The drive cable of the Ferris wheel came off its track and the wheel went into free spin. Initially, midway workers and police officers at the scene tried to unload the riders by controlling the wheel manually, but the load became unbalanced. When the Fire Department Technical Rescue Team arrived on the scene, they attached ropes to each side of the wheel to secure it. One side was tied to a fire engine, and the other to a semi-trailer truck. Once the wheel was secured, the team could bring each set on the ride around for passengers to get off. No passengers were injured in the incident, but two police officers received minor injuries when the wheel broke free the second time. Investigators found that the operator failed to load patrons in a way that balanced the weight across the wheel.

source: Arkansas Dept. of Labor
acc_desc: 10-year-old boy's jacket or shirtsleeve became entangled in the machinery.  The spinning action of the ride pulled the clothing farther into the machinery, eventually pulling the child's whole body out of the car and entrapping him within the moving parts of the machine.  When the ride was finally stopped, the boy's limbs were caught in the gears.
injury_desc: The child was ambulanced to a local hospital, then med-flighted to *** hospital.  No information was provided on the injuries treated or the child's outcome.
notes: Witnesses stated that the wind was blowing hard.  The child riding next to the boy said she felt a jerk and then saw her brother flying out of his seat.  State investigators concluded that the child's arm was outside the car.  According to measurements taken by state inspectors, the distance from the seat to the part of the ride where the clothing became entangled is 17.5 inches.  ASTM F2291, the design standard for amusement rides, requires that designers provide a clearance envelope to keep riders from encountering "hostile features".  Designers are instructed to consider the possibility of a patron extending arms or legs through vehicle openings, and establish the envelope using the maximum reach of a 95th percentile adult plus 3 inches (effectively a 99.9 percentile).  According to Dreyfuss, the arm reach of a 99th percentile man is 31.5 inches, almost twice the distance from the side of the Orbiter car to the entrapment point.  The arm reach of a 10-year-old boy is 22 inches.F2291 exempts all rides designed before 2003 from compliance with modern safety requirements, including the patron clearance envelope.  Therefore the Orbiter is in compliance with industry standards.  State inspectors did not cite the carnival for any safety violations related to the accident, although they did write citations for failing to document ride maintenance, failing to properly document inspections, and failing to post 6 of 7 specific items required by the manufacturer as part of the signage.In 2007, the British Health and Safety Executive published a lengthy report:  "Passenger behaviors on amusement rides", which included a survey of rule-breaking behavior for a wide variety of rides.  An Orbiter ride was observed for 22 minutes (8 cycles, 286 patrons).  During that short time, 2 children were observed reaching an arm outside the carrier.  Observers perceived the motivation for the action differently in each case.  A girl described as younger than 11 extended her arm as a natural pose.  A boy between 11 and 15, was assumed to be motivated by thrill enhancement.  Whatever the motivation, the observation suggests that children are likely to extend their arms from the car of the Orbiter, despite signage instructing them not to.  The short reach envelope designed into the ride makes this a risky action.

notes: State officials performed testing to determine the dimensions of the patron clearance envelope on the coaster. The final test results indicated the clearances to be 17 inches on the left side of the train and 16 inches on the right side. Beyond that, some parts of the ride structure will be struck. The average arm length of an adult male, adult female, and 12-year-old in the 50th percentile is 28.5', 26.2', and 24 inches, respectively. The 16' clearance on the train does not allow for any clearance if the patron were to move their elbow or arm outside of the train car. The park has signage posted to keep hands and feet inside car, keep your back against the seat, brace yourself on all turns, and keep your seat. The patrons do not follow these instructions and have historically raised their hands and arms over their heads and stuck their hands and arms out of the side of the cars while riding.  In 2001, a 45-yo woman hit her arm on something at some point on the incline to the second hill, causing a laceration that required 13 stitches to close.After this second accident, state officials ordered the park to evaluate and modify the attraction to prevent and protect patrons from being able to touch any part of the structure of the attraction while riding.

notes: State officials performed testing to determine the dimensions of the patron clearance envelope on the coaster.  The final test results indicated the clearances to be 8.5 inches on the left side of the train and 12 inches on the right side.  Beyond that, some parts of the ride structure will be struck.  The average arm length of an adult male, adult female, and 12-year-old in the 50th percentile is 28.5", 26.2", and 24 inches, respectively.  The 8.5" clearance on the train does not allow for any clearance if the patron were to move their elbow or arm outside of the train car.  The park has signage posted to keep hands and feet inside car, keep your back against the seat, brace yourself on all turns, and keep your seat.  The patrons do not follow these instructions and have historically raised their hands and arms over their heads and stuck their hands and arms out of the side of the cars while riding.State officials ordered the park to evaluate and modify the attraction to prevent and protect patrons from being able to touch any part of the structure of the attraction while riding.

acc_desc: 3-yo child critically injured in fall from ferris wheel when the tub flipped over due to a combination of operational snafus that resulted in the ride freewheeling.  Child was riding with an adult.  The wheel did not have seatbelts.
injury_desc: Hospitalized in critical condition with multiple injuries, including a skull fracture.
notes: State investigators documented a series of operational snafus involving two operators, alleged-but-unconfirmed misconduct (a sledgehammer in the operator's area may be been used to circumvent the deadman pedal), and what appear to be fundamentally unsafe load/unload procedures. One operator loaded the victim, then turned the ride over to a second operator.  The first operator tested .010 on a blood alcohol screening after the accident.  The operator who relieved him tested sober, but stated that -- on two separate occasions that day -- he accidentally hit the off switch for the hydraulic pumps, then unloaded the ride in such a way that it became unbalanced and began to freewheel.  After the first incident, he was able to turn the pumps on without the wheel freewheeling too far.  The second time, he was unable to stop the motion.  The ramp was still in the up position and the footrests on the cars started hitting the ramp as they traveled forward out of control.  The impact with the ramp caused the victim's car to overturn.  The adult riding with the child said the carrier rotated 360 degrees at least two times, maybe more.  He was able to hang onto the child for the first revolution, but eventually the boy slipped from his grasp and fell to the pavement below.  Conclusion of the state report:  "The investigation has failed to disclose conclusive evidence of ride owner or operator error involved with this accident.  The ride was found to be operating within manufacturers design specifications.  As requested, the investigation file is being forwarded to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) since the Ferris wheel is a mobile amusement ride.  The CPSC gathers information on these types of accidents to investigate and determine if the ride can be made safer."

source: Oklahoma Dept. of Labor
acc_desc: Adult male was ejected from water slide and fell 24 feet to the concrete below.  A power failure caused two of the three water pumps to shut down, which lowered the water level in the slide and caused the patron to slide faster than normal.  The park manager was in his office at the time of the accident and did not notice the water level discrepency until an hour after the accident when he observed that patrons were sliding faster than normal.
injury_desc: Transported to the hospital by ambulance with injuries to ankle
notes: The accident was reported to state ride safety authorities by the victim's family three days after the accident.  State investigators found that there was no documentation of daily inspections, operator training or maintenance log, and the lifeguard training certificate was not on-site.State officials made the following recommendations:1) Install a warning device on the supply motor pumps for the slides to alert maintenance personnel and/or operators in the event of an electrical power outage.2) Provide a mark for the operator to observe at the loading area indicating that there is sufficient water in the slide.3) Provide training for operators and instruct them on the proper way to ride the water slide.4) Provide signage at top slide platform instructing patrons on the proper way to ride.

source: New York Dept. of Labor
acc_desc: Ride attendant was fatally ejected while riding the attraction in an improper and unsafe position.
notes: According to witness statements, the deceased was working as ride crew manager on the Mind Scrambler.  She boarded an open car after loading guests, kneeling backwards rather than sitting properly with her seatbelt latched.  The crew member at the operator controls, whom she was supposed to be supervising, yelled at her to sit down, but then started the ride anyway.  She was swaying and dancing to the music as the ride accelerated.  The lights added to the ride as a safety feature after a 7-yo child was fatally ejected from the same ride in 2004 were only designed to stay on during start up and slow down.  Once the ride reached full-speed the lights went off.  This was the point at which the ride crew supervisor was ejected from her seat and hit repeatedly by the ride. The second operator station installed after the 2004 accident was not manned at the time of the ride operator's death.  Employees reported that it was rarely, if ever, used. Despite the fatal accident on the Mind Scrambler three years prior and the death of another 7-year old child on a different ride at the same park in 2005, the ride owner had never bothered to implement a documented training program or provide operators with written operating instructions required by industry standards. The Mind Scrambler had passed state inspection and satisfied insurance requirements despite the deficiencies.  OSHA investigators might have insisted on mitigation of these chronic problems following the death of the ride operator, but Rye Playland is owned by the county and, therefore, exempt from OSHA oversight.

source: Florida Dept. of Agriculture
acc_desc: 13-yo girl was riding with two other children, leaning head back and laughing, when her head struck another part of the ride.  She lost consciousness with her head back, and her head then struck the handle of the cup next to her.
category: Impact: extremity hit something outside carrier
notes: State ride inspectors re-inspected the ride and found it to be operating per manufacturer's specifications.  Based on operator and witness statements, investigators concluded that the girl became dizzy, sick, and disoriented as a result of the combined efforts of the 3 passengers to generate a high spin rate.  The victim's control over her movements was compromised and she wound up in a postion that put her within striking distance of other parts of the ride.  Centrifugal force from the cup's high rate of speed contributed to the accident, but was not the sole cause.  The victim became dizzy and disoriented, but the other two riders in her car did not.  An unrelated witness reported that the centrifugal force had caused her own children to rise in their seats while riding, but those children did not attain the same dangerous proximity to other parts of the ride that the injured girl did.  The manufacturer's manual does not indicate that any limits are placed on the rate of speed at which a car is allowed to spin, nor does the manufacturer specify a maximum height or weight for patrons on this kiddie ride.  The victim was approximately 115 pounds, 5'2" tall.  One page of the report states that she was 13 years old, another page states that she was 14 years old.

acc_desc: The foot tub of one of the gondolas struck a portion of the structure while 3 patrons were riding in the car.  The collision of the tub and structure shattered the fiberglass foot tub of the gondola.  One of the riders was cut under her eye by the flying debris.
notes: The carnival company did not report the accident to authorities per state law.  The owner/operator continued to operate the ride without determining what caused the gondola to hit the structure.  A state inspector was informed of the accident five days later during a routine inspection of other rides inthe same carnival, when he encountered an investigator from the CPSC onsite.  The injured patron had reported the incident to CPSC.State inspectors found that the ride was being operated without a current permit and the owner had failed to file an updated itinerary until after the accident occurred.  The employee operating the ride had been hired one day prior to the accident and did not have access to the ride manual.  It was discovered that the attraction was being operated with a sweep mounted upside down and with the damaged foot tub.  An order probiting use was put on the ride by state inspectors following the investigation.The state concluding the following:  "It is believed that this accident could have been prevented.  It is also believed that the situations and equipment condition that led to this event had the potential to cause great bodily harm and death."  In all, seven corrective orders were written.  The owner/operator was ordered to hire a licensed engineer to conduct a structural and engineering analysis and inspection of the Whirlybird and conduct repairs to restore the ride to original manufacturer specifications.

source: Arkansas Dept. of Labor
acc_desc: Mother and child were ejected from a Sizzler ride.  The child was killed, the mother injured.
injury_desc: 7-yo boy died from severe injuries to head.  Mother was treated and released.
notes: Ride owner did not report the accident per state law and moved the ride 2 hours after the bodies were removed.  The operator was responsible for operating multiple rides and, at the time the boy and his mother were being ejected, his attention had been diverted by a customer asking to ride the second ride.  The key used to lock the ride's lap bars was missing, so the operator was using a pocket knife to lock the door. Inspection of the ride revealed (quoted from report):The ride had not been maintained according to manufacturer's specifications.  The ride was in need of repair by having worn parts, missing bolts, a broken lap bar, hydraulic leaks and painted hoses and several tub pins that did not move freely.  The ride was found to have numerous tubs with broken or missing fiberglass, wiring that was intended for lights hanging loose and broken or missing light covers. Duct tape had been used to repair fiberglass parts.  It was also found that the operators control panel had been altered by adding a toggle switch to control the ride bypassing the red emergency stop button.The operator's statement confirmed that at the time of the incident, the emergency stop button did not work.  He stated that his supervisor knew about this, but told him to operate the ride anyway.  There was no documentation of his employment or training with Razorback Amusements as required per state regulations and ASTM standards.  It was also discovered that he was not given a fact sheet which is to include information on how to operate the ride, emergency evacuation and other information such as what to do in case of an emergency.Other documentation that was not available included maintenance records, maintenance schedule, inspection checklist, or daily pre-operational inspections.  In total, state safety authorities found 10 violations and 47 instances noted, and recommended corrective actions.

acc_desc: Patron was riding on a single tube.  At the first turn, he jammed his leg on the top of the slide and then heard a snap.
category: Impact: hit something in participatory attraction
notes: State officials investigated a series of similar accidents on this slide.  This attraction has sweeps, bumps, and 90-degree turns that simulate a raft going up against rocks and traveling down white water. The Division could see that at the 90-degree turn, the bottom of the attraction is beveled to make the front of the raft go up the wall, and not directly into the wall, allowing the rider?ÇÖs feet to swing away from the wall of the attraction. When they hit the wall with their feet hanging over the front of the tube, one badly sprained her ankle, and two dislocated their ankle. The Division also found that all of the injured were wearing some type of shoe or footwear while traveling down the attraction. Wearing footwear on this attraction could allow the foot to stick to the side of the slide because the slide is made of concreteand has a rubber-covered foam covering the concrete. This would cause excess force to be placed on the rider?ÇÖs foot, causing damage to the foot.State officials ordered the park to prohibit riders from wearing footwear, to change the max weight for a single tube rider from 250 to 200 pounds, and to change the front riding position on all multiple tubes so that the front rider sits with legs crossed instead of hanging over the front of the tube.

notes: State officials observed that when a double tube comes into contact with the center island, located in teh bowl, the tube has a pattern of rising up at an angle and flipping over.  This does not appear to happen with any of the single tubes.  Since there were multiple injury accidents of this type, state officials, with cooperation of the park, determined that only single tubes would be utilized until the park modifies the attraction by creating bumpers for the side wall of the island and the exit wall.State officials inspected the modifications on June 15, 2007 and approved the slide for operation with double tubes.

source: California Division of Occupational Safety and Health
acc_desc: Patron was riding in a triple tube with 2 friends when they crashed into a wall.  He hit his right foot and dislocated his ankle.
category: Impact: hit something in participatory attraction
notes: State officials investigated a series of similar accidents on this slide.  This attraction has sweeps, bumps, and 90-degree turns that simulate a raft going up against rocks and traveling down white water. The Division could see that at the 90-degree turn, the bottom of the attraction is beveled to make the front of the raft go up the wall, and not directly into the wall, allowing the rider?ÇÖs feet to swing away from the wall of the attraction. When they hit the wall with their feet hanging over the front of the tube, one badly sprained her ankle, and two dislocated their ankle. The Division also found that all of the injured were wearing some type of shoe or footwear while traveling down the attraction. Wearing footwear on this attraction could allow the foot to stick to the side of the slide because the slide is made of concreteand has a rubber-covered foam covering the concrete. This would cause excess force to be placed on the rider?ÇÖs foot, causing damage to the foot.State officials ordered the park to prohibit riders from wearing footwear, to change the max weight for a single tube rider from 250 to 200 pounds, and to change the front riding position on all multiple tubes so that the front rider sits with legs crossed instead of hanging over the front of the tube.

acc_desc: Patron was riding on a double tube with her friend.  While going around the first bend in the slide, she felt her foot get caught between the raft and the wall.  As the raft turned, she felt a pop.
injury_desc: Badly sprained ankle.  Transported via ambulance to local hospital.
category: Impact: hit something in participatory attraction
notes: State officials investigated a series of similar accidents on this slide.  This attraction has sweeps, bumps, and 90-degree turns that simulate a raft going up against rocks and traveling down white water. The Division could see that at the 90-degree turn, the bottom of the attraction is beveled to make the front of the raft go up the wall, and not directly into the wall, allowing the rider?ÇÖs feet to swing away from the wall of the attraction. When they hit the wall with their feet hanging over the front of the tube, one badly sprained her ankle, and two dislocated their ankle. The Division also found that all of the injured were wearing some type of shoe or footwear while traveling down the attraction. Wearing footwear on this attraction could allow the foot to stick to the side of the slide because the slide is made of concreteand has a rubber-covered foam covering the concrete. This would cause excess force to be placed on the rider?ÇÖs foot, causing damage to the foot.State officials ordered the park to prohibit riders from wearing footwear, to change the max weight for a single tube rider from 250 to 200 pounds, and to change the front riding position on all multiple tubes so that the front rider sits with legs crossed instead of hanging over the front of the tube.

The discrepency in reports triggered an investigation.  See report for more details.

acc_desc: Patron's raft failed to make it up the first incline after being dispatched.  The patron injured her lower back when she slid over the outlet jets in the slide's surface while sliding back into the first dip.
injury_desc: Bruising to back.  Transported by ambulance to local hospital.
notes: During the past year, state officials had received a total of five injury reports concerning this attraction.  All five injuries were related in that they have occurred when the water flow for the attraction has not be adequate due to a variety of reasons.  All resulted in patrons moving backwards down an incline after not being able to reach the top.  Due to the chronic history of this problem, state officials initiated an investigation (see report).When questioned as to whether the problems had been reported to the manufacturer, per industry standards and state law, the owner/operator did not recall whether there existed any correspondence with the manufacturer.  The owner/operator indicated that they believed the manufacturer to be out of business.  State officials asked for records of the installation inspection required by the manufacturer; the park could not produce documentation and had no recall of the manufacturer's inspection.State officials contacted the slide manufacturer (very much still in business) for assistance with the injury pattern on this slide.  The manufacturer provided the state with a copy of the installation inspection report (the report the owner/operator failed to produce or recall).  The tendency of riders to collide on this slide was discussed in the report, as were a number of other issues relevant to the problem.  Recommendations had been made to the owner/operator (see attached), but not adopted.  The report was issued by the manufacturer in 2001, and numerous patron collisions had occurred in the five years since.  The state issued four requirements to the park, ordering them to peform an extensive hazard analysis of the ride and submit a plan for mitigating the risk of collision.

acc_desc: 6-year-old child riding alone in Giant Wheel panicked when the ride stopped while his car was near the top, climbed over the seat, and fell 70-80 feet to his death.
notes: The Giant Wheel is 90 feet tall with 20 open gondolas.  Patrons are not secured to their seats in any manner, and there exists no physical barrier on the gondola that would prevent a patron from exiting.  The manufacturer's minimum height limit for unaccompanied riders is 42".  The deceased was 49" tall and had just graduated from kindergarten.State regulators issued a corrective action specification requiring that the Giant Wheel attraction be evaluated and modified to prevent and protect passengers from being separated from the ride while it is in operation.  The evaluation shall include a thorough hazard analysis and shall control resulting risk of falls from height.  Signage and patron instructions alone will not be considered sufficient to comply with the intent of the requirement.

acc_desc: Two patrons were dispatched on the slide in a tube.  While they were still within the slide area, an off-duty lifeguard on his work break went down the slide prior to being dispatched by the slide operator.  The solo slider collided with the two riders, knocking one of them from their tube.
injury_desc: Pain to upper right thigh.  Transported by ambulance to local hospital.
notes: Numerous witness statements were gathered by the park regarding this and another similar accident that occurred 3 days prior.  All statements agreed.  State officials found that the primary cause of the accidents was the improper control of the patrons by the slide operator.  After the collision accident three days prior, state officials ordered the park to add a second operator at the top of the slide to better control dispatching.  At the time of this accident, there were two operators at the top of the slide.  However, because the rider that dispatched himself early was another employee, the slide operators were not concerned he would dispatch early.State officials ordered the park to develop and implement a procedure to ensure that riders cannot be dispatched without the previous riders being clear of the slide.

acc_desc: The ride attendant was loading the ride when he heard a child crying. He went over to the car. He discovered that possibly the child's finger was pinched when the seat belt was fastened. Everything seemed to be OK. Then, the ride was run full cycle. Everyone was unloaded and to the ride attendant's knowledge, there was no injury. The ride was still in service until approximately 12:10pm when we were told that Jonah Mason received some type of hand injury and that his mother had taken him to the hospital emergency rooom. At that time, the ride was shut down and the NJ Department of Community affairs-Bob(area supervisor). He was given the information that we had aboutl the incident. At the time of the report, we were unsure of the exient of the injury. Per NJ Department of Community Affairs, ride was re-inspected and put back into service at 12:50pm. Loading and operating procedures were also observed and checked out to be satisfactory. Upon recieiveing telephone call from Autumn Mason at approximately 1:45pm, we received the correct information and address and telephone number. We believe that Jonah pinched his finger when he buckled the seat belt. He then moved his hand quickly and bumped it somewhere in the car. As the patron's tube approached the narrowing area of the slide, the tube collided with the side bumper.  This impact knocked the patron from the tube.  The patron was not involved in horseplay and was riding properly.  As the inspector watched, a number of other patrons struck these bumpers; some were knocked from their tubes. source: New York Dept. of Labor
acc_desc: Seven-year-old child boarded water dark ride by himself while his mother waited outside.  Investigators surmised that he left his boat, fell into the waterway, and was crushed between two submerged conveyors.  Operators told investigators that a boat came back around a short while after the boy boarded with only a wet shoe in it.  The operator removed the shoe and continued operating the ride.  The child's mother noticed that the same cars had made several loops and her child still hadn't emerged.  The ride was shut down and a search began for the boy.  He was found dead approximately 30 minutes later.
injury_desc: Child was crushed between two underwater conveyors and died of a head injury.
notes: Operator statements indicate that two of the four ride attendants had left their posts on the ride to get water shortly before the child boarded, leaving the crew short-staffed.  A 3rd party audit of park operations performed the summer before this accident recommended that "a policy be developed and enacted concerning eating or drinking while on duty as a Ride Operator or attendant...Ride operators/attendants leaving their position, at their own discretion, to purchase soft drinks and candy from vending machines (oftentimes leaving one operator or less than is specified at the ride location) and then consuming the snacks while the ride is operating is a practice that should not be tolerated."The state report included operator training records for two unnamed operators; both tests showed (different) incorrect answers to a question asking what the minimum height limits were.  Both incorrect answers were marked correct by the trainer. State regulators issued a notice of violation and order to comply with the following:1) Provide a guard and/or electronic trip-wire for space between conveyors.  Guard shall protect ingoing nip points.  Trip-wire shall shop conveyor immediately when activated.2) Assure that there is a minimum of four(4) operator on ride at all times of operation.3) Provide a height limit sign that is clearly visible to operator or ticket taker.  Sign shall be in plain site and used to load ride.

source: New Jersey Dept. of Community Affairs
acc_desc: At approximately 9:30pm on Sunday July 24, 2005 a woman came into our Guest Services office with a complaint about the High Seas. This woman was alone, with an empty baby stroller in her hands. This woman stated that her daughter was on the High Seas ride. While the ride was in motion her daughter some how was able to slide under the lap restraint. This woman, who I will now call the mother, stated that she yelled to the ride operator to stop the ride, but the ride operator did not hear her. The mother then went on to state her concerns about the safety of the ride and for her daughter. I listened carefully to the mothers concerns, and offered her a 6 ticket refund for the ride for both her and her daughter, which she graciously accepted. T then told her that I personally was going to go to the High Seas and speak to the ride operator about the incident, in which I did. After speaking with the ride operator, I found out the following. The mother and daughter were in boat #3. The mother was facing the sling shot ride, while the daughter was facing the ride operator. At the time of the incident, all 4 boats were in operation. While the ride was in motion the ride operator was watching all 4 boats. While watching the boats, an man tapped her on her shoulder as she heard the mother yelling 'stop'. The ride operator then hit the stop button for all 4 boats. While the ride was stopping, the mother proceeded to remove the daughater from her seat and place her in her arms. When the ride came to a complete stop, the ride operator went over to boat number 3. At this point, both mother and daughter were on the same side of boat(facing sling shot). The ride operator then asked if everything was ok, and the mothers response was 'I think this ride is not for us, I think we will choose something else.'
injury_desc: Ride operator at this point assisted both passenger off of the ride and gave the mother a six ticket refund for their ride. At approximately 10:30-11:00pm, the ride operator was on sweeping duty around the park, and saw the mother put her daughter on the NASCAR ride. The ride operator stated that both were smiling and happy, and that there was no sign that either were upset about the earlier incident on the High Seas.
category: Fall: patron fell off inner tube, mat or board

acc_desc: Patrons went to ride the Tilt-A-Whirl ride. As they approached a car, patron began to open a lap bar. Before patrons could enter the car, the ride started. Since they were not seated, and the ride began its cycle, patron pulled her daughter to the stationary platform that surround the ride. Patron yelled to the operator to stop the ride. The ride eventually came to a stop. The Male ride operator told patron that he made a mistake. Daughter's upper left arm was in pain. Ice was administered. As per Operator, he was working the Tilt-A-Whirl ride. He left the ride to drop off a pen at the adjacent ride swings. When he returned, he saw the lady on the exit platform facing the Mardi Gras. The lady said something to him, which he did not understand, he asked her to repeat herself, and she said an accident happened where she had to pull the girl's arm. Operator told the lady that it was a mistake and that we were sorry. As per Borislav, Nadya let the customers enter the Tilt-A-Whirl ride. He witnessed Nadya unlock the brakes. Nadya went to start the ride when Borislav saw the customers were not seated,( the girl had the lap bar opened and was about to get in and the mother was on the stationary cat walk.) when the brakes were released the mother ran down and grabbed the girls arm since the cars began to freely spin. The mother puled the daughter to the stationary platform. Borislav, took Nadya's hand away from the start button (so they could not start it ) and applied the brake. The mother and daughter initially did not appear to be set, because they got in the seat and wanted to ride. However, Borislav is an assistant manager. He was recently promoted to this position from ride operator. At the time of the incident he was a certified operator on the ride, revealing the other operator (who needed a pen). The girl running the ride was an operator in training.

source: New Jersey Dept. of Community Affairs
acc_desc: As per patron, he was riding the Pharaoh's Fury ride. He was sitting in row #1 by himself. As the car descended from its peak on the left side, (patron's side) the lap bar pulled out of its housing. At the time, patron was holding onto the lap bar.When the lap bar came loose, patron positioned his feet to secure himself in the seat. As the boat passed the fencing, the lap bar caught the fence on the platform. This motion pinched his right forearm between the wrist and elbow on the underside of his arm. Patron was taken to the 'Guest Relations' office where ice was administered, and this report was taken. As per ride operator, Rafal Bury, the patron and another passenger were sitting on opposite sides of the boat in the end seats. Rafal said patron was yelling and gripping the lap bar tight. When the lap bar came out, Rafal removed his foot from the 'dead-man' pedal and pressed the 'emergency break' button. As per Assistant Manager, Daniel Sierra, who witnessed the incident, the patron was riding in row #1 on the 'Pharaoh's Fury' ride. Patron was clutching his lap bar as the ride began to run its cycle (Swinging side to side). The ride was in its beginning stage and not making a full swing. His lap bar appeared to pop out on the left side. patron continued to hold onto the lap bar, causing it to become positioned perpendicular from its normal position. Daniel then witnessed the operator disengage the 'Dead-Man' switch. Patron was standing in his seat holding onto the lap bar. The lap bar moved around from the left side of the boat to the outside of the right side. Patron was still holding onto the lap bar when it hit a section of fence surrounding the platform on the ride's lift side (same side as patron). The lap bar broke off when it struck the platform fence.

acc_desc: Lap Bar plunger causing bolts loosened and casing with plunger came off the side of the car while the train was running around the track. Lap bar and rotor mechanism stayed in place. Train and guest went through nomal ride cycle and unloaded at the station area. It appears that all 6 bolts that hold the casing on became loose and fell out allowing the casing to come off the train. We believe it is possible that the bolts were incorrectly tightened during the assembly process from the winter rehab. After checking all other casing mechanisms on both trains it appeared to be an isolated occurrence. We reinspected each lap bars rachet casing bolts on both trains and reinstalled that one that came off. All devices were inspected prior to the ride reopening. We have requested from Philadelphia Toboggan to allow us to change from the current star lock washer to a two tab washer on these 6 bolts. source: Massachusetts Dept. of Public Safety
acc_desc: Woman reached top of inflatable climbing wall and began to descend.   She apparently lost her grip and fell.  The line attached to her harness was held by the operator at a point before the line fed through the gri-gri mechanism.  As the woman lost her grip, the force of her falling pulled the rope from the operator's hands which allowed her to *** to the base of the device.  When she hit the base of the Rock Wall, she struck her head on the asphalt curbing, resulting in a fatal injury.
injury_desc: Fatal head injury.  Patron lost consciousness at scene, was transported to the hospital and died four days later.
category: Fall: in climb or play area
notes: State inspectors found the safety equipment to be in proper working order after the accident, however the operator/attendant had not been properly trained in its use.  In particular, the operators were not trained to hold a patron's harness rope at a point after it had traveled through the gri-gri, and were not trained to pull the slack rope after the gri-gri so that the gri-gri would clamp the rope and prevent a patron from falling.  Because the operator was not properly trained, he incorrectly took up the slack of the rope before the gri-gri, thus enabling the victim to free fall when the rope pulled from the operator's hands.The owner/operator was cited for:  1) failing to properly license and permit the device; 2) no notification of itinerary; 3) failure to train operators in proper operation of device; 4) failure to provide the operator/attendant with manufacturer's manual; and 5) failure to follow manufacturer's specifications.

acc_desc: Two females were injured on the *** log Flume ride owned by ***.
injury_desc: Both were transported to local hospital, the 21 year old lost her upper tooth with cuts and bruising to mouth and possible fractured jaw. The 14 year old received bruises to forehead and left arm.
notes: Inspection revealed that one of the sensors that control flow of carriers had been sticking during operation that day. This allowed too many carriers to log jam at the base of the first hill, this then makes the ride stop as it is intended to do. Supervisor stated that ride operator physically by-passed the sensor causing ride to start again bringing down the carrier before water level had risen. Higher water level acts as a breaking motion for carriers when dropping down hill to lower flume section. Carrier reached the bottom with low water level making carrier ram into side of flume causing patrons to strike side of carrier. Malfunctioning sensor was replaced with retraining of ride operator by supervisor. Ride was re- inspected and reopened by the bureau. An Administrative Complaint will be filed against the ride owner as a result of the findings.

source: California Division of Occupational Safety and Health
acc_desc: When train was released from the station it did not engage the chain at the bottom of the lift hill.  The train rocked back and forth and then suddenly engaged the train.
injury_desc: 5 patrons suffered whiplash-like conditions and were transported to local hospitals.
notes: State investigators concluded that the chain skipped as the chain dog tried to connect with the chain.  The anti-rollback devices failed to work as designed, however the ARB failure was secondary to the chain dog failure.  Owner/operator stated that this failure had happened before when oil from the chain was allowed to collect in the area between the chain dog and its housing (the chain dog sometimes sticks and does not drop freely).  The problem continues to happen despite daily cleaning.  State inspectors were unable to view the condition of the equipment at the time of failure because the owner/operator had cleaned and oiled the chain prior to notifying Division inspectors.  Letters from two California Registered Engineers were presented indicating that no changes were necessary in the existing chain dog system.  Both engineers agreed that "the function of the locking mechanism is quite sufficient to continue as is - providing that it is kept in a free moving and well-lubricated condition".  The daily inspection checklist has been updated to reflect this additional requirement.

acc_desc: On July 17, the mother of an unknown aged male child called this office complaining that a set of loose car keys in the floor board of the bumper car she and her son had been in had fallen through a hole in the floor.  She initially wanted to know if there shouldn't have been warning signs about not dropping or carrying keys in the ride.   After further questioning she advised the keys were hers and had been around her wrist on a coil spring type wrist key chain and her car key had been destroyed by the electrical arch when the wheel rolled over it (power is derived from a wheel instead of stinger pole on these bumper cars.)  And she'd had to incur expenses for a locksmith and a new car key.
injury_desc: When asked if her son was injured she advised her son had been burned on the leg by the sparks and when asked if he was transported to the hospital she said she'd taken him to the hospital.  Follow up investigation and inspection determined the woman initially wanted an immediate $200 from the operator to have a locksmith come and open her car and make her another key.  She later reduced the amount to $100.  The operator denied payment and later assured our Inspector that there had been no injury claimed at any time the woman or her son were at the facility and no mention was made of her taking the boy to a hospital.
notes: A follow up inspection found no discrepancies, the hole in the floor board is a manufacturer's drain hole found on all of the tubs however, with out inspector's concurrence the operator took steps to cover these holes with screen to prevent this from happening again.

source: California Division of Occupational Safety and Health
acc_desc: Patron was traveling down the slide on a double tube with her husband.  When they turned a corner, she fell out of the tube, striking her head on the slide and causing her to lose consciousness.
notes: Victim told state investigators that she and her husband were sitting upright in the tube when they started traveling faster and the tube went up on the side wall of the slide.  At that point, she just fell out.  The combined weight of the two riders is approximately 380 pounds.  Time tests of the slide showed that a tube with heavier patrons (combined weight 400 lbs) traveled down the slide an average of 5 seconds faster than a tube with lighter patrons (combined weight 250 lbs).State inspectors reviewed the operational procedures and performed an inspection.  Nothing was found physically wrong with the slide, but the inspectors did not hear the operators give the proscribed verbal instructions (lean back and hold the raft handles) to any of the guests prior to dispatch.  A requirement was written ordering the operators to give the safety talk to each guest prior to dispatch.  The purpose is to position the rider's center of gravity closer to an even plane with the slide.  In doing this there would be less chance of roll outs/overs on the slide.

His left leg was still sticking through the left side of the restraint, but the rest of him was sliding through the right side.  The parents yelled to the operator to stop the ride.  The child was able to hold on for a while.  When the ride slowed and the chairs got closer to the ground, the father tried to grab the child. source: Prescott Valley (AZ) Police Department
acc_desc: 22-year-old woman died while riding Sizzler carnival ride, approximately 60 seconds into the ride cycle.
injury_desc: Coronor could not determine cause of death, but said most likely cause was cardiac arrythmia.  Tissue sections revealed very few disease processes.  She was significantly overweight.  "It is further noted that this young woman was recently delivered of a full term infant.  One could reasonably imply that the decedent MAY have had relative iron deficient anemia secondary to that pregnancy.  There may also have been lingering fluid redistributions associated with her post partum state such that centrifugal forces produced during the ride may have altered blood flow to the brain.  All of these ride-related physiologic changes are but speculative at best and clearly not proven."
notes: Arizona has no ride inspection or investigation program, so the ride owner was allowed to self-inspect and reopen the ride 45 minutes after the death.  The victim's mother told police that she "observed the ride in the first minute and made mention to the operator three times that the ride was too fast and that she thought it was faster than she'd ever seen".  No public safety agency in Arizona had authority to shut the ride down pending an independent RPM check.

source: Rhode Island Building Commission
acc_desc: One of the camshafts that cause the horses to go up and down broke out of its seat next to the gear.  Once freed from the circular motion, the horses proceeded to travel on a tangential path, causing the camshaft to slide away from the center of the ride and hit the spreader beam.  The spreader beam fell on a mother who was holding her child.
injury_desc: Mother was transported to the hospital.  Preliminary x-rays showed no broken bones, but an MRI was ordered to confirm.
notes: State investigators found that the ride was being operated without cotter pins to secure bolts as required by manufacturer's instructions.  Corrective actions were:  1 - require that all amusement rides must have cotter pins (or r-keys for portable rides) in all the holes located in the bolts on which spreader beams sit; 2 - owners of carousels must obtain maintenance requirements from manufacturers and must know the tolerances of wear.

notes: The lap bar is a metal bar with a metal loop located at each end.  The metal loops allow the bar to slide up and down over the chains that hold the seat in place. source: California Division of Occupational Safety and Health
acc_desc: Operator inadvertently started the ride while 3 children were being loaded into a car, before the attendant had secured the boys' safety bar.  The load attendant clung to the front of the car and was lifted up as the car rose.  His weight imbalanced the car, causing it to tip up and eject the three boys from a height of 10 feet.  The loading attendant then let go of the car and fell to the ground without injury.
injury_desc: 8-yo boy broke both wrists.  Report does not state whether he was admitted.  The other two children were treated for minor injuries and released.
notes: During the initial conversation following the accident, the ride owner told state officials that three boys fell a few feet onto grass and showed no sign of injury.  Based on the owner's description of a non-injury event, the inspector verbally released the ride to operate.  Yet in a statement released by the Fair the same day, one of the minors was listed as being treated for 2 broken wrists.  The state's investigation concluded that ride operator accidently hit the jog switch with his elbow during a shift change, causing the car to move before the children were secured.  In order to prevent another incident in the future, the state ordered that the jog switches "be of a constant pressure type and fully guarded".  In addition, the owner was ordered to install and operator-presence switch.

notes: During unannounced inspection, state officials observed another occurence of a patron being knocked from their tube.  As the patron's tube approached the narrowing area of the slide, the tube collided with the side bumper.  This impact knocked the patron from the tube.  The patron was not involved in horseplay and was riding properly.  As the inspector watched, a number of other patrons struck these bumpers; some were knocked from their tubes. acc_desc: This ride has 4 speed slides. The guard at the top dispatches all 4 slides and waits for them to clear before dispatching the next 4 riders. Just before this incident occurred, the lifeguard dispatched all 4 slides. The guest on slide #8 did not go down the slide with the other riders. The guard walked over to speak with the guest and told her to "go" several times. In the meantime, it seems that a 10 year old girl who does not speak english boarded slide #7. When she heard the lifeguard instructing the other rider to "go" she went down the slide, but the lifeguard did not see this. The guard waited for the girl on slide #8 to clear the catch pool before dispatching the next group. The girl in slide #7 took longer to go down the ride and was not clear when the next group dispatched. She was struck by a 14 year old boy a she was exiting the catch pool. She complained of back pain and was taken to the hospital for observation.
injury_desc: Complained of back pain.  Transported to ER.
notes: DOSH required ride owner to install mechanical device at entrance to dispatch area for crowd control.

source: Connecticut Dept. of Consumer Protection
acc_desc: 5-year-old girl forcefully ejected from a kiddie coaster as her car rounded last curve on the 1st trip of the cycle, landing on her head.  The girl was sitting in the 3rd car, left-hand side.
injury_desc: Transported via ambulance to hospital.  Cat scan and x-rays were negative.  Sustained facial lacerations and bruises.
notes: Investigators observed the coaster in operation and found that it did not appear to slow down as it came around the last curve where the accident occurred.  Investigators also noted that, while the safety bars worked as designed, there is only one setting which is sized large enough to allow adults to ride.  Consequently, the safety bar would allow a child to move and bounce around in the seat or even bounce up with the force of the ride.  State investigators found that the Downhill Air Pressure Brake Regulator control, used to control a slowdown brake, was missing.  Ride operator stated that he didn't know what the device was and had never been trained to use it, even though he'd been working for Strates Shows for over a year.  The Kiddie Ride Manager for Strates Shows stated that the device hadn't been in use for over a year, and he didn't know why.  Note:  NY Dept. of Labor investigated another accident on this same coaster citing the slow-down brake and inadequate lap bar design.

notes: Owner/operator did not report the accident as required per state law.  The child's mother called the Division two days later.  The child stated that she reached for her toes as the ride approached full speed in an effort to turn herself upside down.  She stated that others were doing the same thing and she believed it was an acceptable riding position.  The protective panel at the top of the couch that is supposed to prevent riders from slipping behind the seat may have been damaged.  By the time state authorities were notified about the accident, the ride had been moved out of state.  An inspection was not possible until 2 months later, at which point the protective panels had all been brought up to spec.

Butler Amusement's maintenance supervisor stated that the rides are inspected once a week, but records showed that the ride had not been inspected during the 5 months prior to the accident. The ride operator's BAC was 0.162%, more than twice the legal limit for automobile drivers in the state of California.

source: Illinois Department of Labor
acc_desc: A woman was injured after the coupling pin between two Himalaya cars came out.  The first car after the disconnected hitch rotated around the sweep arm and ended up bottom side up under the second car.  It was fortunate that these cars were not occupied.  The fourth car, the one in which the woman was riding, did not get damaged during the incident.  The investigation revealed that in order for the connecting pin to come out, an 'R' key would have to have been lost or removed from the end of the pin.
notes: Illinois state regulators have suggested to the manufacturer that the pins be changed.  At present, the pins are inserted from the outside of the circle with the 'R' key on the inside.  When used in this manner, centrifugal force tends to pull the pin to the outside of the circle and against the 'R' Key.  If the design were changed, centrifugal force would tend to keep the pins in, even if the 'R' Key were lost.
